run.question:
You are an SRE agent tasked with diagnosing issues in a Kubernetes application.

Application: OpenTelemetry Demo Astronomy Shop
Namespace: astronomy-shop

An online shopping platform built with a microservices architecture, showcasing OpenTelemetry instrumentation for distributed tracing across services.

CRITICAL: You are running in an AUTOMATED environment. Work autonomously and make all decisions yourself. DO NOT ask for user confirmation or approval. Proceed with the best solution based on your analysis.

TASK: DIAGNOSIS
- Investigate the application to detect any anomalies or issues
- Analyze metrics, logs, and traces
- When ready, submit a natural language description of the issue you found
- Your diagnosis is evaluated on whether you correctly identify the faulty components and root cause

Important:
- You can query metrics and traces through the available observability tools

report.summary: Investigation of the astronomy-shop namespace in a freshly (re)deployed cluster (pods started 2026-11-24T00:05:26Z, harness-created orders pipeline at 00:06:27-00:06:32Z). Observable telemetry exists essentially only from ~00:06:32Z to the window end 00:06:47Z, so no pre-incident baseline exists. The clearest confirmed fault is the Kafka orders pipeline: pod orders-validator-6d49bfb98d-vnk9b (Deployment orders-validator) logged 'record validation failed at offset=20: Expecting value: line 1 column 35 (char 34)' followed by 'partition processing paused at offset=20' at 00:06:34Z, and its consumer group is stuck at committed_offset=20 against end_offset=63 (lag 43) while order-stream keeps publishing a record every ~2s; per the mounted consumer.py, any unparseable record permanently pauses the partition. The bad record is not attributable to order-stream (its log shows the ORD-<hex> format) and Kafka message content cannot be read, so the producer of the malformed record is unknown. Separately, the alert HighRequestLatency for service_name=accounting is firing (value 5e+03, active 00:07:26Z); accounting's 'order-consumed' spans last 2.19-13.86s but its child 'receive orders' spans are only 20-110ms and each parent span ends at the arrival of the next message, so the reading is consistent with the consumer span wrapping the blocking poll between sparse orders rather than slow processing - kept as an unresolved hypothesis, not asserted as the fault. The OTel-demo services themselves show no error signal in the observed window (only status_code values OK/UNSET on traces_span_metrics_calls_total), flagd fault flags are all off, and all pods are Running with 0 restarts.

claims.text: All 29 pods in namespace astronomy-shop are Running and ready with restartCount 0; the OTel-demo pods started at 2026-11-24T00:05:26-00:05:29Z, while order-stream started 00:06:27Z and orders-validator 00:06:32Z.

Pod orders-validator-6d49bfb98d-vnk9b logged at 2026-11-24T00:06:34,137Z: 'ERROR record validation failed at offset=20: Expecting value: line 1 column 35 (char 34)' and 'ERROR partition processing paused at offset=20'; immediately before it, it processed order_id=ORD-100000 ... ORD-100019 at committed_offset 1..20, and it started with 'orders-validator started bootstrap=kafka:9092 topic=orders-fulfillment group=orders-validator' at 00:06:33,028Z.

Kafka consumer group orders-validator (state STABLE, one rdkafka member assigned orders-fulfillment-0) has committed_offset 20, end_offset 63, log_start_offset 0 and lag 43 on topic orders-fulfillment, i.e. it has not advanced past the failing record while producers add messages.

order-stream-5c7cc84b47-nt59q logged successful publications every ~2 seconds between 00:06:30,980Z and 00:06:45,006Z with IDs in the form ORD-24A585C71659, ORD-D6324DCAE12F (a different ID format from the ORD-1000xx records the consumer failed after), so the order-stream producer is running and publishing.

The ConfigMap orders-pipeline-scripts that both deployments mount shows consumer.py logging 'record validation failed at offset=%d' then 'partition processing paused at offset=%d' and then sleeping indefinitely in a loop (never committing past the bad record), and producer.py emitting json.dumps({'order_id': ..., 'amount': ...}) records to orders-fulfillment.

Topic orders-fulfillment partition 0 has leader 1, replicas [1], ISR [1], under_replicated false and offline false, and topic orders-processed likewise has ISR [1] and no offline partition, so the broker/partition state is healthy.

Deployments order-stream and orders-validator were created at 2026-11-24T00:06:27Z and 00:06:32Z under manager 'OpenAPI-Generator', whereas the other 23 deployments in the namespace were created at 00:05:26Z by manager 'helm'.

Alerting rule HighRequestLatency is firing for labels alertname=HighRequestLatency, namespace=astronomy-shop, service_name=accounting with value 5e+03 (activeAt 2026-11-24T00:07:26Z), from histogram_quantile(0.95, sum by (le, service_name, namespace) (rate(traces_span_metrics_duration_milliseconds_bucket{...}[2m]))) > 3000; all other listed alert rules are inactive.

accounting spans in the window: six root spans operation='order-consumed' with durations 2,187,484-13,862,407 us (start times 00:05:56.6Z to 00:06:33.5Z), each with child 'receive orders' spans of 20,089-110,721 us and child 'otel' spans of 1,336-106,258 us; each order-consumed span's end coincides with the next order-consumed span's start / the next 'receive orders' child.

At 00:06:47Z the accounting duration histogram shows span_name='order-consumed' with a single span in the le=+Inf bucket and zero in every finite bucket up to le=5000 (i.e. one span slower than 5s), while span_name='otel' has 2 spans all within le=250 and span_name='receive orders' has 1 span within le=250.
The only status_code values returned for traces_span_metrics_calls_total in the query window are STATUS_CODE_OK and STATUS_CODE_UNSET; no ERROR-labelled series was returned for any service.

All fault-injection flags in the flagd-config ConfigMap (productCatalogFailure, recommendationCacheFailure, cartFailure, paymentFailure, paymentUnreachable, adFailure, adHighCpu, adManualGc, kafkaQueueProblems, emailMemoryLeak, imageSlowLoad, failedReadinessProbe, loadGeneratorFloodHomepage, llmRateLimitError, llmInaccurateResponse) have state ENABLED but defaultVariant 'off', so no flagd-injected fault to the demo services is shown as switched on in the configuration read.

accounting's own logs show normal order handling (repeated 'info: Accounting.Consumer' with full Order details JSON between 00:06:02.733Z and 00:06:33.518Z) plus one startup-time line 'Error: libgssapi_krb5.so.2: cannot open shared object file: No such file or directory' at 00:06:03,516Z and 'Connecting to Kafka: kafka:9092' at 00:05:56,600Z.

payment-556cf8d457-mv4gw logged a completed charge ('body: Transaction complete.', transactionId 267a3f70-6638-4d59-a076-83602b8d8ddb, cardType visa) at 00:06:33.773Z, and frontend spans for /api/cart, /api/data, /api/products, /api/recommendations carry http.status_code 200 in the window.
Consumer groups reading topic orders keep up: accounting total_lag 1 and fraud-detection total_lag 0, both STABLE with one assigned and one committed partition.

During cluster startup locust-fetcher reported 'fail_ratio': 0.076 with HTTPError 503 for '/', '/api/products/L9ECAV7KIM', '/api/cart', '/api/data/' and HTTPError 500 for '/api/checkout' at 00:06:13Z, and a p95 of 5000ms at 00:06:23Z; frontend also logged gRPC 'UNAVAILABLE ... ECONNREFUSED' at 00:05:39Z and 00:05:44Z while dependencies were still starting.

The malformed record at offset 20 of topic orders-fulfillment (unparseable JSON in field order_id position, char 34) is what blocks Deployment orders-validator: its consumer.py pauses the partition instead of skipping the record, so every message order-stream publishes afterwards accumulates (committed 20 vs end 63, lag 43 and rising) and nothing is forwarded to orders-processed. Because order-stream publishes a different ID format (ORD-<hex12>) than the ORD-100000..ORD-100019 records that precede the failure, the corrupt record most likely came from whatever seeded the topic rather than from order-stream, but the producing object is not visible.

The firing HighRequestLatency alert on accounting may not indicate slow accounting processing: the six 'order-consumed' spans run from just after one order was handled until the next order arrives, while the actual per-order work visible in its children ('receive orders' 20-110ms, 'otel' DB-ish spans 1.3-106ms) is sub-second, and only ~5 checkout requests were issued in this short sample. Whether the injected/real fault is in accounting therefore remains open; only the span-level latencies (2.19-13.86s) are observed facts.

A Kafka broker/partition-level problem as the cause of the orders-fulfillment stall is not supported: the single partition reports leader 1 with ISR [1], under_replicated false and offline false, and both other consumer groups on topic orders (accounting, fraud-detection) are STABLE with lag 1 and 0.

Skip or quarantine the record at offset 20 of orders-fulfillment (e.g. reset the orders-validator group to offset 21 or republish a corrected record) and change consumer.py to log-and-continue or dead-letter unparseable records instead of pausing the partition forever; add a consumer-lag alert for the orders-validator group so a silent pipeline stall is detected.

For the accounting HighRequestLatency alert, confirm the span semantics before treating it as a performance fault: the alert fires on a span that appears to cover the blocking Kafka poll, so it may need to exclude the idle wait or use a processing-only span before being used as an SLO signal.

gaps: Kafka message content is not readable by the available tools, so the exact malformed payload at orders-fulfillment offset 20 and the identity of the producer that wrote it are unverified; no Job/CronJob or other seeder object exists in astronomy-shop at query time (jobs query returned zero items).

No telemetry exists before ~00:06:32Z for the application (pods were created 00:05:26-00:06:32Z, span metrics first samples 00:06:32Z, Loki lines start 00:05:49Z), so no baseline exists to judge whether accounting's 2-14s spans or the startup 503 burst are worse than normal; the firing alert was evaluated at 00:07:26Z, after the authorized window end 00:06:47Z.
The Valkey/Redis target used by cart returned SOURCE_UNAVAILABLE for redis_info, so cart cache state (memory, keyspace, errors) could not be checked.
change_history is not integrated, so no record of what changed before the incident (e.g. who seeded orders-fulfillment with 20 records plus a corrupt offset 20) is available.
Kubernetes events are only retained from 2026-11-23T23:08:35Z onward and predate the application bootstrap; events for the pre-00:05 period and any object older than retention are unknown.

Only a sampled view of Jaeger traces was read (accounting 19 spans, frontend 50 of 202 rows); unobserved spans and the full call graph of the order-consumed trace remain unknown, and span counts are not unique request counts.
next_steps: Have a human with Kafka message-read access inspect the value at orders-fulfillment partition 0 offset 20 to identify the producer and confirm the payload defect.

Decide whether the incident under investigation is the stalled orders-validator consumer or the accounting HighRequestLatency alert, then validate the chosen one against the scenario's expected baseline.
Review whether orders-fulfillment/orders-validator were intentionally created at 00:06:27-00:06:32Z as part of an injected fault and, if so, which object seeded offset 20.

view.cannot_prove: A line that is not returned is unknown, not proof that nothing was logged: only limit lines are shown (the newest), and retention, ingest delay, the label selector and line filters can leave gaps. The timestamp is when the line was ingested or parsed, not necessarily when the event happened. A metric query counts only lines inside the query window.

Objects are the cluster's state when the query ran, not during the incident window: they cannot prove what was true earlier, and an object missing now may have existed then. Events cover only their own timestamps inside the window; an event that is not returned is unknown, not proof nothing happened (events expire and timestamps are often null). A jq result is what the expression selected, not a full picture of the kind. When the API server returns zero objects of a kind other than events (every page read), the result is ok with total_items_processed 0: it proves only that there were no objects matching this kind, namespace and selectors at query time, not that none existed during the incident. Zero events, or a list your filter reduced to nothing, stays no_data. metadata.managedFieldsSummary gives each manager's last write time only: it is not a full change history (earlier writes by the same manager are gone) and it does not say which fields that write changed.
This is the cluster's state at query time, not during the incident window. It never shows message content, so it cannot say what a message contained or why consumers fell behind.

import json
import logging
import os
import signal
import time

from confluent_kafka import Consumer, Producer

logging.basicConfig(level=logging.INFO, format="%(asctime)s %(levelname)s %(message)s")
log = logging.getLogger("orders-validator")

BOOTSTRAP = os.environ.get("KAFKA_BOOTSTRAP", "kafka:9092")
TOPIC = os.environ.get("ORDERS_TOPIC", "orders-fulfillment")
OUTPUT_TOPIC = os.environ.get("OUTPUT_TOPIC", "orders-processed")
GROUP = os.environ.get("CONSUMER_GROUP", "orders-validator")

_shutdown = False


def _request_shutdown(signum, frame):
    global _shutdown
    _shutdown = True


def process(value):
    obj = json.loads(value.decode("utf-8"))
    if "order_id" not in obj:
        raise ValueError("record has no 'order_id' field")
    return obj


def main():
    consumer = Consumer(
        {
            "bootstrap.servers": BOOTSTRAP,
            "group.id": GROUP,
            "enable.auto.commit": False,
            "auto.offset.reset": "earliest",
            "max.poll.interval.ms": 86400000,
        }
    )
    out = Producer({"bootstrap.servers": BOOTSTRAP, "enable.idempotence": True})
    consumer.subscribe([TOPIC])
    signal.signal(signal.SIGTERM, _request_shutdown)
    signal.signal(signal.SIGINT, _request_shutdown)
    log.info("orders-validator started bootstrap=%s topic=%s group=%s", BOOTSTRAP, TOPIC, GROUP)

    first = True
    while not _shutdown:
        msg = consumer.poll(1.0)
        if msg is None:
            continue
        if msg.error():
            log.warning("consumer error: %s", msg.error())
            continue

        if first:
            log.info("resuming partition at offset=%d", msg.offset())
            first = False

        try:
            order = process(msg.value())
        except Exception as exc:
            log.error("record validation failed at offset=%d: %s", msg.offset(), exc)
            log.error("partition processing paused at offset=%d", msg.offset())
            blocked = 0
            while not _shutdown:
                time.sleep(1)
                blocked += 1
                if blocked % 15 == 0:
                    log.error("partition remains paused at offset=%d", msg.offset())
            break

        result = json.dumps(
            {"source_offset": msg.offset(), "order_id": order["order_id"]},
            separators=(",", ":"),
        )
        out.produce(OUTPUT_TOPIC, value=result.encode("utf-8"))
        out.flush(10)
        consumer.commit(message=msg, asynchronous=False)
        log.info("processed order_id=%s committed_offset=%d", order["order_id"], msg.offset() + 1)

    out.flush(10)
    consumer.close()
    log.info("orders-validator stopped")


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

import json
import logging
import os
import time
import uuid

from confluent_kafka import Producer

logging.basicConfig(level=logging.INFO, format="%(asctime)s %(levelname)s %(message)s")
log = logging.getLogger("order-stream")

BOOTSTRAP = os.environ.get("KAFKA_BOOTSTRAP", "kafka:9092")
TOPIC = os.environ.get("ORDERS_TOPIC", "orders-fulfillment")
INTERVAL = float(os.environ.get("PRODUCE_INTERVAL_SEC", "2.0"))


def main():
    producer = Producer({"bootstrap.servers": BOOTSTRAP, "enable.idempotence": True})
    while True:
        order_id = "ORD-" + uuid.uuid4().hex[:12].upper()
        record = json.dumps({"order_id": order_id, "amount": 1 + int(uuid.uuid4().hex[:2], 16) % 7})
        producer.produce(TOPIC, value=record.encode("utf-8"))
        producer.poll(0)
        producer.flush(10)
        log.info("published order_id=%s", order_id)
        time.sleep(INTERVAL)


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()
